first.text:
Honestly, nothing in the sessions themselves. Wednesday's negatives and band pull-ups, Sunday's band pull-ups and Friday's strict single are set for set the same as before. Nobody adds a rep or changes a band because of this.

What changes is how your week is judged afterwards:

- **The pull-up work is finally watched.** Until now the only thing counted toward the pull-up was the one strict single, so a week where you skipped Wednesday entirely still looked like a full pull-up week. From now the negatives and band sets count toward a target of 10 a week. Do the week as written and you land at 11; lose Wednesday and you land at 4, and the check-in will say the pull-up fell short, not that it was fine.
- **Three short weeks in a row gets a response.** If the pull-up comes in under 10 in three of four weeks, the weekly plan flags it and I owe you a fix: usually putting the missed sets somewhere else, not just noting it.
- **A disrupted week has an easier floor.** When illness or travel cuts the week down, each main lift still has to keep a couple of hard sets. Band pull-ups now satisfy that for the pull-up, so a cut-down week can keep the band work and skip the strict single rather than the other way round.
- **One less thing I have to explain every version.** The old "target of 1" needed a written justification each time; a real target doesn't.

So: same training, truer scorecard. The thing to feel is that a missed Wednesday now shows up as a pull-up gap, which is exactly what it is.

Ready to adopt on your yes.
